plain_english_summary:
For Langford elections and assent votes, the bylaw sets how electors register and vote, including advance, special and mail voting, and how ballots are counted. It also sets when and where political signs and advertising are allowed.

Key rules:
- Advance voting is from 8 am to 8 pm on the 10th day and the 3rd day before general voting day.
- A mail ballot must reach the Chief Election Officer before the close of voting on general voting day to be counted.
- Political signs may only be placed after the start of the campaign period and must be removed within 48 hours following the election or assent voting.
- Political signs may be placed on private property only with the property owner’s permission, and not within 2 metres of a fire hydrant.
- Political advertising and signs are prohibited within 100 metres of a place where voting proceedings are being conducted.
- Political advertising must not be scattered, dropped or broadcast from any vehicle in operation, including aircraft and other aerial vehicles.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to people voting in City of Langford elections and assent voting, and to people placing political signs or advertising within the City.

Mobile home parks in Langford’s electoral area must meet rules for permits, layout, safety, services and maintenance. Residents need the park operator’s written permission and a building permit before starting additions or separate buildings on a space.

Key rules:
- A park permit is required before establishing, constructing, altering or subdividing a mobile home park.
- Maximum density is 8 mobile home units per acre; each mobile home space must be at least 3500 square feet.
- Skirting must be installed within 30 days of a mobile home’s installation on its pad.
- Tenants must first obtain a letter of permission from the park operator and then a building permit before construction of additions or separate structures.
- The initial park permit application fee is Twenty-five Dollars ($25.00) for the first space and Ten Dollars ($10.00) for each additional space.
- A violation can result in a penalty not exceeding one thousand dollars ($1,000.00), plus prosecution costs; each continuing day is a separate offence.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to mobile home park owners and operators, tenants, and park applicants in Langford’s electoral area.

The bylaw sets fees for City services and charges listed in its schedules, including administrative, finance, planning, mapping and RCMP services. Fees in Schedules A, B, C and D automatically adjust each year on May 1 based on the annual change in the Greater Victoria All-Items Consumer Price Index (CPI).

Key rules:
- Schedules A, B, C, D and E are replaced by the schedules attached to the amendment.
- Fees in Schedules A–D adjust every May 1 by the annual percentage change in the Greater Victoria All-Items CPI for the most recently ended calendar year.
- The CPI is the figure published by Statistics Canada or a successor in function.
- The text marks Schedules A–D as superseded; their listed fees are not the updated rates.

Who it affects: It applies to people and organizations that use City services or request documents, information, maps or RCMP services subject to the fees.

Protected Trees on any property in Langford generally cannot be cut, removed or damaged unless an exception applies or the City issues a Tree Permit. Permits can require replacement trees, security and protective measures during construction; violations can lead to fines and replacement requirements.

Key rules:
- Protected Trees include trees with a DBH equal to or greater than 20 cm, plus several other categories listed in the bylaw.
- A Tree Permit is valid for one year; emergency removal requires an application on the next business day.
- Outside designated Environmentally Sensitive areas, replacement ratios range from 1:1 to 1:3; trees over 90 cm require a biologist replanting plan.
- Replacement Trees must be planted within 1 year; security is $400.00 per Replacement Tree.
- Work within five (5) metres of a Protected Tree’s trunk generally requires a Tree Protection Barrier.
- Unlawful cutting, removal or damage can require 3 Replacement Trees per tree within 30 days; the minimum fine is $5,000.

Who it affects: It applies to anyone dealing with Protected Trees on any property in Langford, including property owners and people doing work there.

The bylaw sets the rules for how land and water areas in Langford may be used or subdivided, where buildings and structures may be placed, and how parking, loading, screening and landscaping are handled. It is organised into parts covering definitions, general compliance and regulations, parking and bicycle rules, how zones are established, and rules for individual zones; schedules include the zoning map and additional area-specific regulations.

Key rules:
- Land use, subdivision, buildings, structures and signs must be permitted by this bylaw or the City of Langford Sign Bylaw.
- The City may enter regulated property at a reasonable time to check compliance.
- Obstructing an enforcement officer or designated person is prohibited.
- Offences may result in a fine up to the maximum under the Offence Act; each continuing day is a separate offence.

Who it affects: It applies to people who own or occupy land or the surface of water in Langford, and to development and activities covered by the bylaw.

Subdivision and development in Langford must meet City requirements for arranging, designing and building highways and services, with the aim of supporting orderly development suited to its intended use and in harmony with the environment. The bylaw is organized into schedules covering procedures and fees, general requirements, earthworks, roads, drainage, sewage, water, utilities, irrigation, construction standards, drafting, parks and trails, and boulevard landscaping.

Key rules:
- Applies to all Langford lands, except applications made before the bylaw came into force and completed within 12 months of adoption.
- Subdivision approval or a building permit requires the owner to provide required works and services on the adjacent highway, up to its center line.
- Final subdivision approval requires Construction Acceptance or a Works and Services Agreement with the City.
- A servicing agreement requires security equal to 100% of the estimated works and services cost, certified by a Professional Engineer.
- During the one year warranty period, developers must remedy defects and provide security of 10% of the actual works and services cost.

Who it affects: It applies to landowners and applicants proposing subdivision or development in the City of Langford.

Alarm systems need a permit, and repeated false dispatches can lead to fees and police not responding to later alarms. Alarm businesses must try to verify an alarm and contact someone responsible for the premises before reporting it to police.

Key rules:
- Alarm permits are free, except an unpermitted system that causes a false dispatch is charged a $25.00 permit fee.
- After three false dispatches from one system in any twelve (12) month period, the occupier receives a notice.
- The fourth and each subsequent false dispatch in any twelve (12) month period costs $100.00.
- After five (5) or more false dispatches in any twelve (12) month period, police may stop responding to subsequent alarms.
- Appeal a false-alarm determination in writing within ten (10) days of being notified.
- A violation of the permit requirement can result in a fine of not less than $100.00 and not more than $2,000.00.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to alarm system users and occupiers of premises with alarm systems, as well as alarm businesses that report alarms to police.

Park visitors must follow park hours and posted notices, protect park features, and avoid activities such as unauthorized camping, fires, sales, or cannabis smoking. Organized events require a City park permit and $5 million liability insurance; violations can result in removal of belongings and fines.

Key rules:
- All Schedule “A” parks are closed between 5:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m.
- No overnight camping, except qualifying temporary shelter use by a homeless person when no accessible overnight shelter is available.
- A permitted temporary shelter must be removed before 7:00 a.m.; size and location restrictions apply.
- Dogs are not allowed on sports fields; dogs on playgrounds or public beaches must be leashed, subject to stated exceptions.
- Organized park events require a park permit and written proof of 5 million dollars liability insurance.
- A bylaw offence can carry a fine of not more than $10,000; each day a contravention continues is a separate offence.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to people using Langford parks, trails, beaches, and other public places covered by its rules.

Businesses operating in Langford must hold a business licence, and the licence only covers the named business and the premises or locations listed. The bylaw sets application and fee requirements, rules for particular business types, and penalties for violations.

Key rules:
- A separate business licence is required for each business and each Langford premises.
- Licence fees are paid in advance; annual fees are not refunded when a business stops operating.
- A transfer fee for a change of premises or a new licence after a change of owner is $10.00.
- Most licences are perpetual and do not expire unless suspended or the licensee reports that the business has ceased operations.
- A person found guilty of an offence may face a maximum penalty of $5,000.00 for each offence.

Who it affects: It applies to people and businesses carrying on business in Langford, including businesses based elsewhere that perform work or services in the District.

Sets Langford’s financial plan for 2005–2009, including projected revenues and spending, and establishes a tax exemption program intended to encourage hotel and motel development in designated areas. The program offers eligible developments an exemption from some general municipal property taxes, subject to conditions and limits.

Key rules:
- The plan balances projected revenues and expenses at $33,038,437 in 2005, $27,719,033 in 2006, $25,068,757 in 2007, $28,399,687 in 2008, and $26,797,537 in 2009.
- Eligible hotel development must be in a designated revitalization area, be classified as Class 6, have a building permit issued in 2004, be valued at a minimum of $1.5 million, and have at least 60 rooms.
- The exemption is limited to the increase in assessed value during construction and may cover general municipal property taxes on eligible buildings; it does not cover utility user fees, parcel taxes, or taxes collected for other governments.
- The maximum exemption term is five years. Applications must be made to the City Treasurer on or before August 31 in the year before the first exemption year.
- For subdivided hotel properties, each unit must be in a bona fide rental pool or hotel management agreement and available for short-term public occupancy at least 182 days per calendar year.
- Motel properties cannot be strata titled or otherwise subdivided; each unit must be available for short-term public occupancy at least 182 days a year throughout the exemption term.

Who it affects: The financial plan applies to Langford, and the tax exemption program applies to owners or applicants for qualifying hotel or motel developments in designated revitalization areas.

The City’s Local Government Engineer decides frontage improvement requirements for subdivision and building permit applications under the conditions set out in the bylaw. Applicants can appeal the engineer’s decision to the Transportation and Public Works Committee, with the required documents and fee.

Key rules:
- Subdivisions creating one or more new lots can require full frontage improvements under Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000, 2010.
- Outside the core area, permits creating one or two new residential units cap required improvements at 5% of building permit work value.
- Permits creating three or more new residential units cap required improvements at 15% of building permit work value.
- In the core area, permits creating one or two new residential units cap required improvements at 20% of building permit work value.
- Qualifying commercial, industrial or institutional building work caps required improvements at 20% of building permit work value.
- Appeals must be filed within 30 days and include an engineer’s estimate, site plan, grounds and supporting evidence, and a $200.00 fee.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to people applying for subdivisions or building permits that may require frontage improvements.

People cannot occupy certain properties used for controlled-substance activities until required safety inspections, repairs, cleaning and certifications are complete, fees are paid, and the Building Inspector removes a “Do not occupy” notice. The bylaw also prohibits unsafe alterations and nuisance conditions, and lets the City inspect properties, require corrective work and recover costs from owners or occupiers.

Key rules:
- Owners must complete required remediation within fourteen (14) days after the City delivers a section 5.6(b) letter.
- A registered titleholder who inspects a tenancy property and discovers a contravention must notify the Building Inspector within 24 hours.
- A property subject to section 4.2 cannot be used or occupied until section 4.3 requirements are met and the “Do not occupy” order is removed.
- Inspection fees are $500.00 per inspection and $500.00 for a special safety inspection; an additional $500.00 applies to a subsequent inspection after an ordered action is not completed.
- An additional administration and overhead fee of 15% applies to Schedule A items (1) to (6); other service fees are charged at actual cost.
- A bylaw offence carries a fine not exceeding $10,000.00; each day of a continuing offence is a separate offence.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to owners and occupiers of properties in Langford, and to anyone whose actions or use of a property are covered by its rules.

The bylaw adopts Langford’s financial plan for 2006–2010 and sets up a revitalization tax exemption program for qualifying hotel and motel development in designated areas. The program can exempt some general municipal property taxes for a limited period, but it does not exempt utility user fees, parcel taxes, or taxes collected for other governments or public bodies.

Key rules:
- Eligible development must be in a designated area, classified as Class 6, and have a building permit issued in 2004.
- The building permit application must show a minimum value of $1.5 million and at least 60 rooms.
- Apply to the City Treasurer by August 31 in the year before the first exemption year.
- The exemption may last up to five years and is limited by the increase in assessed value.
- Hotel or motel units must be available to the public for short-term occupancy for at least 182 days per calendar year.
- The exemption does not cover utility user fees, parcel taxes, or taxes imposed by other governments or public bodies.

Who it affects: Hotel and motel developers and property owners seeking a revitalization tax exemption in Langford areas where hotel or motel use is permitted.

Get a soil permit before removing or depositing soil in Langford unless an exemption applies. The bylaw limits work hours, sets permit fees and expiry periods, and requires soil work to avoid hazards and protect waterways and nearby land.

Key rules:
- Less than 100 cubic metres total per calendar year on or from one parcel is exempt from the permit requirement.
- Permitted work may occur from 7:00 am to 7:00 pm, Monday to Friday, except statutory holidays.
- Class A permit fee: $250; Class B: $65 administration fee plus $0.50 per m3 of soil.
- Class C: $100 plus $0.50 per m3 (maximum $3000); D: $100 plus flat fee of $3000; E: $500 per operation.
- Permits expire after 90, 120 days or 1 year, depending on permit class; extensions are limited by soil volume.
- Unpermitted soil must be removed or replaced within seven days’ notice; the maximum fine is $10,000.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to people removing or depositing soil on land in Langford, including landowners and Commercial Soil Enterprises.

Keep silt and substances harmful to fish and aquatic life out of Langford’s watercourses, ditches and drains. Owners and occupiers must maintain stormwater systems and silt or petroleum separators so these pollutants are not discharged from their land.

Key rules:
- Maintain silt or petroleum separators in proper working order.
- Maintain stormwater collection and disposal systems to prevent harmful discharges.
- Do not discharge silt or substances harmful to fish or dependent aquatic life into a watercourse, ditch or drain.
- The maximum fine is $10 000; each day an offence continues is a separate offence.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to landowners and occupiers with the specified stormwater systems or separators, and to anyone who might discharge prohibited substances into a watercourse, ditch or drain.

Taxable property in Langford was charged 2006 taxes for municipal purposes, regional and regional hospital purposes, and municipal debt. The amount depended on the property’s assessment class and the rates in the attached schedule; a parcel’s minimum tax was One Dollar ($1.00).

Key rules:
- Tax rates are stated in dollars per $1000 of taxable value.
- Rates vary by property class and by levy, as set out in Schedule ‘A’.
- Sewer debt taxes apply to taxable property in Sewer Specified Area No. 1.
- The minimum taxation on a parcel of real property is One Dollar ($1.00).
- The levies are for the year 2006.

Who it affects: Owners of taxable property subject to the listed 2006 municipal, regional, hospital, or debt levies.

Taxable properties are charged 2008 municipal and other listed property taxes at rates that vary by property class. The bylaw also sets a minimum tax of $1.00 per parcel.

Key rules:
- Rates apply to taxable assessed land and improvements for the year 2008.
- Rates are stated as dollars of tax per $1000 taxable value and vary by property class.
- The schedule sets rates for municipal, Regional District hospital, Regional Hospital District, Sewer Specified Area No. 1 debt, and general debt purposes.
- The minimum taxation on a parcel of real property is One Dollar ($1.00).

Who it affects: Owners of taxable property in Langford, including property in Sewer Specified Area No. 1.

Drivers must stay at or below 30km/h on the roads and road sections listed in the bylaw, with a stated 40km/hr limit on a specified section of Leigh Road. Non-arterial and non-collector roads in the Westhills Development are also limited to 30km/h and must have traffic-calming features.

Key rules:
- The 30km/h limit applies to the roads and road sections named in section 1.
- Leigh Road: 40km/hr from Costin Avenue, south of Goldstream Avenue, through the intersection, to the ambulance station at 2764 Leigh Road.
- In the Westhills Development, roads other than Arterial or Collector roads have a 30km/h maximum speed.
- Westhills roads covered by that limit require traffic-calming features constructed to the satisfaction of the City Engineer.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to people driving or operating motor vehicles on the specified roads in Langford.

For 2005, the bylaw sets property tax rates on taxable land and improvements to fund municipal, regional hospital, sewer-area debt and general debt purposes. Rates vary by property class and are stated per $1,000 of taxable value; the minimum tax on a parcel is $1.00.

Key rules:
- 2005 rates apply to the assessed value of taxable land and improvements.
- Rates are dollars per $1,000 taxable value and vary by property class.
- Residential rates: municipal 3.0734; Regional District 0.5991; Regional Hospital District 0.2606; sewer debt 0.1768; general debt 0.2614.
- The sewer-area debt rate applies in Sewer Specified Area No. 1.
- Minimum taxation on a parcel of real property: One Dollar ($1.00).

Who it affects: This bylaw applies to taxable land and improvements in Langford; the sewer-area debt levy applies to property in Sewer Specified Area No. 1.

For 2007, the bylaw sets property tax rates for municipal purposes, regional hospital purposes, regional district hospital purposes, Sewer Specified Area No. 1 debt, and general debt. The rates depend on property class, and the minimum tax on a parcel of real property is $1.00.

Key rules:
- Rates are stated as dollars of tax per $1,000 taxable value.
- Residential rates: General Municipal 2.3184; Capital Regional District 0.4375; Regional Hospital District 0.2045; Sewer Debt 0.1003; General Debt 0.1699.
- Rates vary across the listed property classes: Residential, Utilities, Major Industry, Light Industry, Business/Other, Managed Forest, Recreational/Non Profit, and Farm.
- The minimum taxation on a parcel of real property is One Dollar ($1.00).

Who it affects: Owners of property taxable for the listed purposes in Langford for the year 2007.

Sets Langford’s revenue and spending plan for 2009–2013 and identifies areas where hotel or motel projects may qualify for revitalization tax exemptions. The exemptions have eligibility limits and do not cover utility user fees, parcel taxes, or taxes imposed by other governments.

Key rules:
- Hotel/motel exemption eligibility requires Class 6 land and a building permit issued in 2004.
- Eligible projects must be valued at a minimum of $1.5 million and have a minimum of 60 rooms.
- Apply to the City Treasurer by August 31 in the year before the first year of exemption sought.
- The exemption term is limited to five years.
- Permissive exemptions are capped at 1/2 of 1% of total municipal property taxes; applications are due August 31st each year.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to Langford taxpayers, organizations seeking permissive tax exemptions, and owners proposing eligible hotel or motel developments.

Taxable land and improvements in Langford were taxed in 2010 for municipal purposes and the other purposes listed in the bylaw. The amount depended on the property class and the rates in Schedule A, expressed per $1,000 of taxable value.

Key rules:
- Schedule A sets rates for eight property classes and five purposes: municipal general, Regional District hospital, Regional Hospital District, Sewer Specified Area No. 1 debt, and general debt.
- Rates are stated as dollars of tax per $1,000 taxable value.
- The minimum tax on a parcel of real property is One Dollar ($1.00).

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to taxable land and improvements in Langford for the year 2010.

Sets Langford’s financial plan for 2019–2023 and explains the City’s revenue and property tax policies. It guides how the City plans to fund services and projects, including its approach to taxes, fees, borrowing and tax exemptions.

Key rules:
- Schedule A adopts the City’s Consolidated Five Year Financial Plan for 2019–2023.
- Except in extraordinary circumstances, tax increases are kept to cost of living or less.
- Various fees are reviewed every 1-5 years to assess whether they recover service costs.
- Council reduces the business property class multiple by 0.05 each year, aiming for 2.5 by 2026.
- Permissive tax exemptions may be considered for organizations showing community access at a nominal charge and community benefit in the previous year.
- Eligible buildings may receive a five-year or 10-year revitalization tax exemption.

Who it affects: The plan applies to the City of Langford and its residents, property owners and municipal service users.

Fireworks sales are prohibited, and fireworks use is tightly limited: consumer and display fireworks require a permit, while consumer fireworks may generally be discharged only on October 31st during the permitted hours. The bylaw also sets permit deadlines and fees, safety requirements, and fines for violations.

Key rules:
- No person may sell fireworks or buy, possess, store, discharge, or use firecrackers or prohibited fireworks.
- Consumer and display fireworks require a permit; applicants must be eighteen (18) years of age or older.
- Consumer fireworks may be discharged only on October 31st between 5:00 p.m. and 10:00 p.m., except for policy-approved exceptional circumstances.
- Consumer permit applications are due by 12:00 p.m. on October 31st, or by 12:00 p.m. on the last business day before it; the fee is $10.00.
- Display fireworks applications are due at least thirty (30) days before the event; the permit fee is $75.00 and insurance must be at least $5,000,000.00 per occurrence.
- A person convicted of an infraction may face a fine of not less than $100.00 and not more than $10,000.00; ticket fines vary by offence.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to people who sell, possess, use, or permit fireworks on property in Langford, including permit applicants and event organizers.

The bylaw adopts Langford’s financial plan for 2007–2011 and creates a revitalization tax exemption program for qualifying hotel and motel development in designated areas. The exemption applies to specified municipal property taxes on eligible building value; it does not remove utility fees, parcel taxes or taxes collected for other governments.

Key rules:
- Eligible development must be in a designated area, classified as Class 6, and have a building permit issued in 2004.
- The development must be valued at a minimum of $1.5 million on the building permit application and have a minimum of 60 rooms.
- Applications must reach the City Treasurer on or before August 31 in the year before the first year of exemption sought.
- The maximum exemption term is five years, subject to the assessed-value increase limit in the program.
- Hotel units must be available for public short-term occupancy for at least 182 days per calendar year; motel units must be available for at least 182 days a year.
- The exemption does not affect liability for municipal utility user fees, parcel taxes or taxes imposed by other governments or public bodies.

Who it affects: It applies to owners and developers of qualifying hotel or motel properties in Langford areas designated for revitalization.

For 2009, property taxes are levied on taxable land and improvements using rates that depend on the property’s tax class. The rates fund municipal, regional hospital, regional hospital district, sewer-area debt and general debt purposes; the minimum tax on a parcel is $1.00.

Key rules:
- Rates are stated as dollars of tax per $1000 of taxable value.
- Residential rates per $1000: municipal 2.1782; regional district 0.3959; regional hospital district 0.2301; sewer debt 0.0567; general debt 0.1300.
- The minimum taxation on a parcel of real property is One Dollar ($1.00).
- The schedule sets different rates for property classes 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9.

Who it affects: Owners of taxable property in Langford in 2009.

The bylaw adopts Langford’s financial plan for 2008–2012 and creates a tax exemption program intended to encourage hotel and motel development. Eligible developments may receive an exemption from some general municipal property taxes, subject to the program’s conditions and limits.

Key rules:
- Eligible hotel development must be in a designated area, be classified as Class 6, and have a building permit issued in 2004.
- The building permit application must value the development at a minimum of $1.5 million, and it must have a minimum of 60 rooms.
- The exemption excludes portions used for retail, bar, lounge, restaurant, meeting, fitness or recreation purposes, and alterations to existing buildings.
- The exemption can last up to five years and is limited by the increase in assessed value and the general municipal property value taxes on eligible buildings.
- Apply to the City Treasurer on or before August 31 in the year before the first year for which an exemption is sought.
- The exemption does not cover municipal utility user fees, parcel taxes, or taxes imposed by other governments or public bodies.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to Langford and to owners or applicants for qualifying hotel and motel developments in designated areas.

The plan sets Langford’s projected revenues and spending for 2010–2014 and establishes a tax exemption program intended to encourage hotel and motel development in designated areas. It also sets limits and an August 31 deadline for organizations seeking permissive tax exemptions; 2010 property tax rates had not yet been set in the plan.

Key rules:
- Permissive tax exemptions are limited to 1/2 of 1 % of total municipal property taxes.
- Permissive tax exemption applications must be received by August 31 each year.
- Eligible hotel development must be valued at a minimum of $1.5 million and have a minimum of 60 rooms.
- The hotel exemption program text requires a building permit issued in 2004.
- Hotel tax exemptions may last a maximum of five years; applications are due on or before August 31 in the prior year.
- Exempt hotel units must be available for public short-term occupancy at least 182 days per calendar year.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to Langford residents and taxpayers, organizations seeking permissive tax exemptions, and hotel or motel developers seeking revitalization tax exemptions.

The bylaw adopts Langford’s five-year financial plan for 2011–2015 and its revenue and property-tax policy disclosure. It sets out the City’s planned revenues, spending, transfers, and approach to taxes, fees, borrowing, and tax exemptions; it does not set 2011 property tax rates.

Key rules:
- The financial plan covers 2011–2015.
- Except in extraordinary circumstances, tax increases are kept to cost of living or less.
- Permissive tax exemptions under section 224 are limited to 1/2 of 1% of total municipal property taxes.
- Permissive tax exemption applications must be received by August 31st of each year.
- The revitalization tax exemption program grants a five-year exemption for eligible buildings.

Who it affects: The plan and disclosed revenue and property-tax policies apply to the City of Langford and its residents, taxpayers, and organizations seeking permissive tax exemptions.

Property taxes for 2011 are levied on taxable land and improvements in Langford, with rates based on the property’s tax class. The levy covers municipal purposes, regional hospital purposes, sewer debt in Sewer Specified Area No. 1, and general municipal debt; the minimum tax on a parcel is $1.00.

Key rules:
- Tax rates are stated in dollars per $1000 of taxable value and vary by property class.
- Residential rates per $1000: municipal 2.1230; regional district 0.3674; regional hospital district 0.2875.
- Residential sewer debt rate is 0.0441 and general debt rate is 0.1159 per $1000.
- Sewer Specified Area No. 1 is subject to the sewer debt rate.
- The minimum taxation on a parcel of real property is One Dollar ($1.00).

Who it affects: Owners of parcels with land or improvements taxable for the listed purposes in Langford.

Sets Langford’s financial plan for 2012-2016, forecasting revenues, spending, borrowing and transfers. It also describes the City’s revenue and property tax policies, including rules for tax exemptions.

Key rules:
- The plan covers 2012-2016 and includes projected revenues, expenditures, borrowing and reserve transfers.
- Except in extraordinary circumstances, tax increases are kept to cost of living or less.
- Various fees are reviewed every 1-5 years to check whether they recover the costs of services.
- Total permissive tax exemptions under section 224 are limited to 1/2 of 1% of total municipal property taxes.
- Permissive tax exemption applications must be received by August 31st of each year and include activity, service-population and financial information.
- Eligible buildings may receive a five-year or 10-year revitalization tax exemption.

Who it affects: It concerns Langford’s municipal finances and affects residents, property taxpayers and organizations applying for tax exemptions.

The bylaw adopts Langford’s consolidated financial plan for 2013–2017 and its revenue and property tax policy disclosure. It sets out planned revenues, spending, borrowing and transfers, and describes the City’s policies for property taxes, fees and tax exemptions.

Key rules:
- Permissive tax exemptions are limited to 1/2 of 1 % of total municipal property taxes.
- Applications for permissive tax exemptions must be received by August 31st of each year.
- Applications must include an activities statement, a description of the group’s membership or population served, and its most recent financial statement.
- Various fees are reviewed every 1-5 years to assess whether they recover service costs.
- Except in extraordinary circumstances, tax increases are kept to cost of living or less.
- Eligible buildings may receive a five-year or 10-year revitalization tax exemption.

Who it affects: The plan applies to the City of Langford’s finances and informs residents, taxpayers, service users and organizations seeking permissive tax exemptions.

The City adopted its five-year financial plan for 2015–2019, setting out projected revenues, spending, borrowing, and transfers. It also records the City’s revenue and property-tax policies, including how it approaches tax increases, fees, debt, and tax exemptions.

Key rules:
- The financial plan covers 2015–2019 and includes the attached schedules A and B.
- Except in extraordinary circumstances, tax increases are kept to cost of living or less.
- Various fees are reviewed every 1-5 years to check that they recover service costs.
- Debt is considered for urgent projects or to leverage grants when internal funding is unavailable.
- Permissive tax exemptions are considered where organizations show community access at a nominal charge and community benefit in the previous year.

Who it affects: The plan applies to the City of Langford and sets financial policies relevant to residents, property owners, service users, and organizations seeking tax exemptions.

Taxable property in Langford was taxed for 2012 using rates based on property class and taxable value. The rates fund municipal purposes, regional and regional hospital district purposes, and municipal general debt; the minimum tax on a parcel is $1.00.

Key rules:
- Schedule A sets rates in dollars of tax per $1000 taxable value.
- Rates vary by property class and cover municipal, Regional District hospital, Regional Hospital District, and municipal general debt purposes.
- The minimum taxation amount on a parcel of real property is $1.00.
- The rates apply for the year 2012.

Who it affects: Owners of parcels with property taxable for the purposes listed in the bylaw.

For 2013, property taxes were levied on taxable land and improvements to fund general municipal purposes, Regional District and Regional Hospital District purposes, and municipal general debt. The tax rates vary by property class and purpose, as set out in Schedule A.

Key rules:
- Rates are stated as dollars of tax per $1000 taxable value.
- Residential rates: General Municipal 2.4303; Capital Regional District 0.5027; Regional Hospital District 0.3192; General Debt 0.1460.
- The bylaw states the minimum tax on a parcel is “One Dollar ($100).”
- The bylaw was adopted on May 6, 2013.

Who it affects: Owners of taxable property in Langford for the 2013 tax year.

Owners of properties served by a sanitary sewer main may have to connect buildings that generate sewage, pay sewer fees, and maintain their private service pipes. The bylaw also sets rules for connection work, septic tanks, sewer use, and fee assistance for eligible households.

Key rules:
- Most sewer-serviced parcels with sewage-generating buildings must connect by the later of one year after main completion and December 31, 2019.
- Specified lakefront parcels must connect within one year after the completion letter or bylaw adoption, whichever is later.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to people applying to the Board of Variance and people whose property is affected by an application.

Development on the lands shaded as Storm DCC Contributing Lands may incur a stormwater development cost charge. - Owners and occupiers must prevent property disrepair, hazards and nuisances; boulevard grass must not exceed 30 centimetres.

- Re-zoned Unoccupied Premises must be demolished within 120 days, unless specified permit or occupancy-ready conditions apply.
- Graffiti must be removed, covered or blocked from public view within 14 days of being placed.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to property owners and occupiers, people in public places, and Developers and Builders working in Langford.

Most new residential developments must provide a share of below-market ownership or rental homes, or pay cash in lieu when the bylaw allows. Affordable homes must meet the bylaw’s price or rent limits and be secured by a Housing Agreement registered on title.

Key rules:
- Market ownership: at least 5% for one-family, two-family and apartments with 5 or more storeys; at least 2% for townhouses and apartments up to 4 storeys.
- Market rental developments must provide at least 10% of their dwelling units as Affordable Rental Housing Units.
- Cash in lieu may replace fewer than ten whole ownership units or fewer than five whole rental units; fractional requirements can be rounded up or partly paid.
- At least 50% of affordable units in a development must have two or more bedrooms.
- Cash-in-lieu charges: $1,387 per new one-family dwelling lot; $1,387 per two-family dwelling unit; $1,355 per townhouse or apartment up to 4 storeys.
- For apartments over 4 storeys, cash-in-lieu charges are $3,689 per Market Ownership Development dwelling unit or $3,862 per Market Rental Development dwelling unit.

Who it affects: Developers applying for residential building permits or subdivision approval in Langford, except where the bylaw’s exemptions apply.

The properties at 3690 and 3694 Happy Valley Rd were moved from the RR4 zone to the RS4 zone, with rules allowing townhouse development subject to specific limits and amenity contributions. At 3690 Happy Valley Rd, subdivision may create a lot of at least 2.7 ha but less than 40 ha without connection to the municipal sanitary sewer system.

Key rules:
- The two properties were rezoned from RR4 (Rural Residential 4) to RS4 (Residential Small Lot 4).
- At 3690 Happy Valley Rd, a lot of at least 2.7 ha but less than 40 ha may be created without municipal sanitary sewer connection.
- Townhouses must follow RT1 zone regulations; more than one residential building is allowed if the buildings contain townhouse use.
- Development on the two properties must not exceed 125 SFE dwelling units; each townhouse unit counts as 0.66 SFE.
- One-family lot contributions: at least 550 m2, $1000 affordable housing and $6000 general amenity; less than 550 m2, $660 and $3960, respectively.
- Townhouse contributions are $610 per unit towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund and $3660 per unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to property owners and development applicants for 3690 and 3694 Happy Valley Rd.

For 2024, property taxes are levied on taxable land and improvements to fund the City’s general purposes, the Regional District, and the Regional Hospital District. The amount depends on the property’s class and taxable value, with rates set per $1,000 of taxable value.

Key rules:
- Residential rates per $1,000 taxable value: municipal 2.41101; Regional District 0.49841; Regional Hospital District 0.12503.
- The minimum taxation on a parcel of real property is One Dollar ($1.00).
- The bylaw sets different rates for property classes 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9.

Who it affects: Owners of taxable property in Langford for the 2024 tax year.

Developers pay amenity cost charges when certain subdivisions are approved or building permits are issued, helping fund recreation centres, community and arts centres, and public-realm improvements. Charges apply across Langford, with exemptions including developments that are not expected to increase the population of residents or workers.

Key rules:
- One-family subdivisions: $3,300 per new lot under 400 m2; $5,000 per new lot over 400 m2.
- Building permits: $3,300 per two-family dwelling unit; $3,050 per townhouse or apartment dwelling unit.
- Commercial or industrial use: $10.75/m2 ($1.0/ft2) of Gross Floor Area.
- Pay when the subdivision is approved or the Building Permit is issued.
- No charge for a complete application submitted before adoption; collected charges are not refunded, but may be credited to a future charge.
- The City may agree to accept an amenity or land instead of payment; the City must approve the arrangement.

Who it affects: It applies to people obtaining specified subdivision approvals or building permits for residential, commercial, light industrial, or general industrial development in Langford.

Shaded portions of 731 Station Ave are rezoned from RM3 (Apartment) to MUM (Mixed-Use Residential Commercial). The bylaw also allows lot coverage on the property to be less than 50% and lists per-dwelling-unit amenity contributions for the property.

Key rules:
- The rezoning applies to the portions shown shaded on Plan No. 1.
- Lot coverage may be less than 50%, despite article (2).
- The listed contribution is $610 per dwelling unit towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund.
- The listed contribution is $1,525 per dwelling unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
- The table lists eligibility for a reduction under Section 2 of Schedule AD, Column 5 of Table 2 only.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to the specified portions of the property at 731 Station Ave.

A portion of 3690 Happy Valley Rd was rezoned from Rural Residential 4 (RR4) to Residential Small Lot 4 (RS4). The bylaw sets amenity contributions for one-family lots and townhouse units on the property, with amounts depending on lot size or housing type.

Key rules:
- The specified portion of 3690 Happy Valley Rd changes from RR4 to RS4.
- One-family lots greater than or equal to 550 m2: $1000 per lot for affordable housing and $6000 for general amenities.
- One-family lots less than 550 m2: $660 per lot for affordable housing and $3960 for general amenities.
- Townhouse units: $610 per unit for affordable housing and $3660 for general amenities.
- The bylaw deletes Subsection 6.13.02(3).

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to the specified portion of 3690 Happy Valley Rd and anyone developing one-family lots or townhouse units there.

The plan guides how Langford’s growth and development should take shape across the entire municipality, covering land use, transportation, housing, climate and infrastructure, ecology, economic activity, food systems, and community services. It is organized into 14 parts of goals and policies, supported by maps and appendices that include development permit area guidelines and environmental and hazard information.

Key rules:
- The Official Community Plan applies to the entire municipality.
- The plan guides decisions but does not itself commit or authorize the City to implement its policies.
- New or amended bylaws and works undertaken by Council must align with the OCP.
- Development permit requirements apply in designated areas; stated exemptions may mean a permit is not required.
- A Development Permit must not vary zoning, use, density, or floodplain requirements.
- DPA application review starts only after full payment of applicable fees.

Who it affects: The plan guides the City’s decisions and affects residents, property owners, and applicants proposing development in Langford.

The City’s adopted financial plan sets out projected revenues, spending, borrowing and reserve transfers for 2025–2029, alongside its revenue and property-tax policies. It identifies property taxes as the City’s primary revenue source and describes how fees, parcel charges, borrowing and tax exemptions are handled.

Key rules:
- The plan covers 2025–2029 and was adopted on May 5th day of May, 2025.
- Various fees are reviewed every 1-5 years to assess whether they recover service costs.
- Parcel Charges are comprised of local area service debt servicing costs for roads.
- Permissive tax exemptions may be considered where an organization shows community access at a nominal charge and community benefit in the previous year.
- The revitalization tax exemption program grants exemptions for eligible buildings for up to 10 years.

Who it affects: The plan applies to the City of Langford and sets out financial and tax policies affecting residents, property owners and organizations seeking permissive tax exemptions.

Langford’s 2026–2030 financial plan sets out the City’s projected revenues, spending, debt payments and transfers, alongside its revenue and property-tax policies. It identifies property taxes as the City’s main revenue source and explains how tax exemptions may be considered.

Key rules:
- Schedule “A” is the City’s Consolidated Five Year Financial Plan for 2026 - 2030.
- Schedule “B” is the City’s Revenue and Property Tax Policy Disclosure.
- Property taxes are projected to provide 50% of revenue in 2026 and 79% in 2029 and 2030.
- Various fees are reviewed every 1-5 years to check whether they recover service costs.
- Permissive tax exemptions may be considered for organizations showing community access at a nominal charge and community benefit in the previous year.
- Eligible buildings may receive revitalization tax exemptions for up to 10 years.

Who it affects: The plan applies to Langford’s municipal finances and informs residents, property taxpayers and organizations seeking tax exemptions.

Parts of 3130 Jacklin Rd are changed from the Neighbourhood and Hillside and Shoreline designations to the Mixed-Use Employment Centre designation. The plan describes that centre as workplace-focused but allows residential and institutional uses, including possible multi-storey, multi-family housing on individual lots.

Key rules:
- The designation change applies to portions of 3130 Jacklin Rd shown shaded on Plan No. 1.
- The Mixed-Use Employment Centre may include commercial, light industrial, residential and institutional uses.
- Multi-storey, multi-family residential buildings may be considered on individual lots without accompanying commercial uses.
- Consideration of those buildings is on a case-by-case or property-by-property basis.
- Housing must not jeopardize the centre’s long-term function as an employment node.

Who it affects: The bylaw affects the specified portions of 3130 Jacklin Rd and people considering land uses or development there.

Specified portions of properties at 2668, 2674, 2682, 2684, 2686, 2696, 2702 and 2706 Sooke Rd are moved into the C9 Community Town Centre Pedestrian zone. The zone allows a mix of residential, retail and other business uses, with rules for building size, pedestrian access, parking and screening.

Key rules:
- The floor area ratio is normally capped at 0.5; eligible land may reach 6.0 if required contributions are paid before a building permit.
- Contributions are $2,074 per new residential unit for the General Amenity Reserve Fund and $610 per new residential unit for the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund.
- Buildings and structures must cover 40% to 90% of the lot.
- Parking and loading must be behind the principal-use building or underground; ground-level parking is prohibited except access to underground parking.
- Principal uses must be designed for pedestrians and avoid interfering with pedestrian movement.

Who it affects: The rules apply to owners and developers of the specified Sooke Rd properties and to people using or living near development on that land.

The listed lands and improvements were exempt from taxation for 2018 and 2019. The exemption applies only to the properties identified in the bylaw, including properties used by named community, religious, charitable and other organizations.

Key rules:
- Tax exemption applies for the years 2018 and 2019.
- The exemption covers only the lands and improvements listed in section 1.
- The bylaw was adopted on October 16, 2017.

Who it affects: It affects the owners or organizations associated with the properties specifically listed in the bylaw.

Portions of two identified properties are moved from the RR4 Rural Residential 4 Zone into the CD12 Comprehensive Development 12 – South Skirt Mountain Zone, as shown on the bylaw’s attached plan. The bylaw also sets a maximum of 2600 residential dwellings across Areas I, II, III, and IV of the CD12 zone, excluding secondary suites, assisted living apartments and care facilities.

Key rules:
- The rezoning applies to the portions of the two properties shaded on Plan No. 1.
- Residential dwellings in CD12 Areas I, II, III, and IV may not exceed 2600 in total.
- Secondary suites, assisted living apartments and care facilities are excluded from the 2600-dwelling limit.
- Schedule X of Bylaw 300 is replaced with the revised plan attached as Schedule B.

Who it affects: The bylaw affects the owners and residents of the identified properties and people in Areas I, II, III, and IV of the CD12 zone.

Businesses that remain open during the COVID-19 pandemic must use distancing measures, limit how many people are inside, and prevent certain customer-handled food and bag practices. These rules apply to business licence holders and carry a fine or penalty of up to $10,000 for each offence.

Key rules:
- Mark entry and checkout lineups every two metres with tape or cones.
- Install secure plexi-glass or plastic barriers at all checkouts.
- Allow no more than one person per sixteen metres squared of floor space open to customers.
- Customers who do not reside together must be kept at least two metres apart.
- Do not use customer-provided containers, reusable bags, or boxes.
- A person who commits an offence is liable to a fine or penalty of up to $10,000 for each offence.

Who it affects: It applies to all businesses in Langford that remain open during the COVID-19 pandemic, and their licence holders.

Permit applicants and holders will pay updated fees for building, plumbing, chimney, fireplace and related permits. The amendment replaces Appendix A of the Building Bylaw with a revised fee schedule, including rules for refunds, re-inspections and fee reductions.

Key rules:
- Building permits for construction valued at $1,000.00 or less cost $58.37; higher values use a tiered fee scale.
- The application fee, included in the building permit fee, is $113.45 for construction valued at $200,000 or less, and $1,134.57 above that.
- Starting work requiring a permit before obtaining the permit doubles the scheduled fee.
- A permit holder who applies to cancel before work starts receives a refund of 50% of the fee paid, but not less than the application fee.
- Necessary subsequent inspections cost $58.37 each; re-inspection fees must be paid before re-inspection.
- The building permit fee is reduced by 5% when the City relies on a registered professional engineer’s or architect’s certification.

Who it affects: People applying for or holding building, plumbing, chimney, fireplace and other permits covered by the revised fee schedule.

The land and improvements at 917 Avrill Road are exempt from taxation for 2018 through 2027 inclusive, provided the property operates as a registered assisted living residence. If it stops being used for that purpose during the exemption term, the exemption ends and the property becomes liable to taxation.

Key rules:
- The exemption covers Roll No. 01-62-327-06001.003 at 917 Avrill Road.
- The tax exemption runs for ten years: 2018 through 2027 inclusive.
- The property must operate as a registered assisted living residence under the Community Care and Assisted Living Act.
- If the property stops being used as specified, the bylaw no longer applies and the property is liable to taxation.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to CCPR Park Residence GP LTD and the specified land and improvements at 917 Avrill Road.

The amendment replaces the application form for an Extraordinary Traffic Agreement and replaces the application form for constructing, using, and maintaining works within a roadway or lane. The new Schedule C includes an expiry date, but the text provided does not state that date or the forms’ detailed requirements.

Key rules:
- Schedule B, Application for Extraordinary Traffic Agreement, is replaced.
- Schedule C, Application to Construct, Use, and Maintain Works Within a Roadway or Lane, is replaced.
- The new Schedule C includes an expiry date; the date is not shown in the provided text.

Who it affects: People applying for an Extraordinary Traffic Agreement or to construct, use, or maintain works within a roadway or lane.

Businesses operating while their licence is suspended or revoked can receive a $500 ticket for either offence. The amendment adds these ticketable offences to Schedule 5 of Langford’s Ticket Information Bylaw.

Key rules:
- Carrying on business while a licence is suspended: section 46(e), $500.
- Carrying on business while a licence is revoked: section 46(e), $500.

Who it affects: This amendment applies to businesses and people carrying on business while a business licence is suspended or revoked.

The bylaw closes a 0.125-hectare portion of the unnamed stub road off West Shore Parkway to public traffic and cancels its status as a public highway. The closure takes effect when the closure plan and other required documents are deposited in the Victoria Land Title Office.

Key rules:
- The closed road covers 0.125 hectares (0.309 acres).
- The affected highway was dedicated by Plan EPP45525.
- The road closes to public traffic when the closure plan and other required documents are deposited in the Victoria Land Title Office.
- The Mayor and Chief Administrative Officer may sign documents needed to complete the closure and disposition.

Who it affects: The closure affects people who use the unnamed stub road off West Shore Parkway and anyone who considers themselves affected by the closure.

Throwing, propelling or casting an axe or knife in Langford is prohibited, except indoors in the stated organized or licensed-business settings. The amendment defines “Axe” and “Knife” and updates the bylaw’s title to include axe and knife use.

Key rules:
- No person may throw, propel or cast an axe or knife within the City, for target or any other purpose, except as allowed.
- Indoor use is allowed as a member of an organized axe or knife throwing Association or League.
- Use is allowed for a customer or client of a licensed business hosting controlled axe and knife throwing events.
- “Knife” includes a spike, shuriken or similar weapon.
- “Axe” can include a hatchet or tomahawk.

Who it affects: The rules apply to anyone throwing, propelling or casting an axe or knife within the City of Langford.

The amendment replaces the sewer bylaw’s Schedule B with a fee table covering 2015–2020. The 2020 entries set charges for sewer connections, capital recovery, storage improvements and sewer use based on water consumption.

Key rules:
- 2020 sewer connection fee: $1500 per inch of service pipe diameter.
- 2020 sewer capital recovery fee: $10497 per R2 equivalent lot.
- 2020 incremental storage improvement fee: $495 per SCRF assessed.
- 2020 sewer user fee: 1.223 per m3 of water consumption.

Who it affects: It affects property owners and sewer utility customers subject to the listed sewer fees.

The property at 957 Walfred Road is changed from the Residential Small Lot 1 (RS1) Zone to the Residential Townhouse (RT1) Zone. The bylaw also sets amenity contributions for each townhouse unit on the property, with no eligibility for a reduction under Section 2 of Schedule AD.

Key rules:
- The rezoned property is Lot 1, Section 84, Esquimalt District, Plan VIP86631, PID No. 027-919-021.
- Amenity contribution: $610 per townhouse unit towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund.
- Amenity contribution: $3,660 per townhouse unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
- The amenity contributions are not eligible for reduction in Section 2 of Schedule AD.

Who it affects: This bylaw applies to the property at 957 Walfred Road and townhouse units on that property.

Businesses covered by the COVID-19 business regulation rules can receive a $500 ticket for any of 12 listed offences. The amendment adds those offences and ticket amounts to Langford’s ticket schedule, and is repealed when the later of two specified emergency declarations is repealed.

Key rules:
- Each of the 12 listed offences carries a $500 fine.
- Offences include failing to mark lineups, install barriers, separate cashiers, or mark aisles directionally.
- Offences include failing to post maximum occupancy signs or exceeding the maximum number of people on the premises.
- Offences include using customer-provided receptacles or selling bulk food items without authorization.
- Offences include failing to maintain 2m physical separation or directional walking measures.
- The amendment is repealed when the later of the March 17, 2020 public health emergency or March 18, 2020 state of emergency is repealed.

Who it affects: It applies to businesses subject to the City of Langford Business Licence and Regulation Bylaw (COVID-19) No. 1907, 2020.

Applicants pay updated fees for Official Community Plan and zoning amendments, development permits and amendments, variances, and temporary use permits. The fee depends on the application and, in some cases, the site area or scale of development; starting work before a required permit is issued doubles the fee.

Key rules:
- Official Community Plan amendment combined fees range from $2,407 for applications concurrent with rezoning to $15,037, based on site area.
- Zoning text amendments cost $3,734 for density-bonus changes or $4,813 for changes to up to two other aspects.
- Waiving a public hearing reduces the marked zoning hearing fee to $2,086; creating a new zone adds $2,281.
- Work begun before permit issuance doubles the fee; interface fire permits cost $301 and riparian permits cost $600.
- Development variance applications cost $1,502; temporary use permits cost $2,105, with renewals at $301.
- Minor amendments reducing a bylaw requirement by no more than 10% cost $240; moderate amendments cost 16% and major amendments 27% of the original fee.

Who it affects: The fees apply to people applying for the planning amendments, permits, and related services listed in the bylaw.

People applying for subdivision, strata, construction and related approvals face the fees listed in a replacement application-fee table. The amendment replaces Table 1 – 1, “Applications and Fees,” in the City’s Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000.

Key rules:
- Residential Statement of Conditions applications: $525 admin fee, plus per-new-lot fees listed in the schedule.
- Commercial or industrial Statement of Conditions applications: $630 admin fee, plus $500 per new lot.
- Boundary Adjustment: $885, plus $250 per each additional lot line to be adjusted.
- A Statement of Conditions extension costs $315 for a 12-month extension; signature expiration or re-signature costs $120.
- On-site construction application: $885, plus 2.5% of the engineer’s estimate up to $200 000 and 1% of the remainder.
- Final subdivision approval: $824, plus per-new-lot fees; DCC payment is due for residential ONLY.

Who it affects: People applying for subdivision, strata, construction or other approvals covered by the application-fee schedule.

Portions of five properties at 1253, 1265, 1277, 1289 and 1300 Valemount Court are redesignated from Hillside or Shoreline to Business or Light Industrial in Langford’s Official Community Plan. The change applies only to the portions shaded on the plan attached to the bylaw.

Key rules:
- The amendment covers five properties on Valemount Court.
- Only the portions shaded on the attached plan are redesignated.
- The designation changes from Hillside or Shoreline to Business or Light Industrial.

Who it affects: The bylaw affects the specified portions of the five properties at 1253, 1265, 1277, 1289 and 1300 Valemount Court.

The bylaw changes the zoning of portions of five properties on Valemount Court to Business Park – Sooke Road West (BP2A), as shown shaded on Plan No. 1. The 1300 Valemount Court portion changes from Attached Housing (RM2A); the other four properties change from Rural Residential (RR5).

Key rules:
- 1300 Valemount Court: Attached Housing (RM2A) to Business Park – Sooke Road West (BP2A), for the shaded portion.
- 1253, 1265, 1277 and 1289 Valemount Court: Rural Residential (RR5) to Business Park – Sooke Road West (BP2A), for the shaded portions.
- The shaded areas are identified on Plan No. 1 attached to the bylaw.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to the specified portions of the properties at 1253, 1265, 1277, 1289 and 1300 Valemount Court.

The five properties at 962, 966, 970, 974 and 978 Bray Avenue are rezoned from One- and Two-Family Residential (R2) to City Centre 1 (CC1). New residential units and commercial space created on these properties are subject to the listed contributions to the General Amenity and Affordable Housing Reserve Funds.

Key rules:
- Per new unit on the 1st to 4th storeys: $2,850 to the General Amenity Reserve Fund and $750 to the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund.
- Per new unit on the 5th and 6th storeys: $1,425 to the General Amenity Reserve Fund and $375 to the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund.
- Per new unit on the 7th storey or higher: $712.50 to the General Amenity Reserve Fund and $187.50 to the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund.
- Commercial space created: $10.75 per square metre towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
- These properties are marked “No” for eligibility for a reduction under Section 2 of Schedule AD.

Who it affects: This bylaw applies to the properties at 962, 966, 970, 974 and 978 Bray Avenue.

Portions of four properties at 3420 Luxton Road, 1120 Finney Road, and 3219 and 3235 Loledo Place are rezoned from RR2 to RS1. The amendment sets amenity contributions for new lots and units on these properties; the contributions are not eligible for reduction under Section 2 of Schedule AD.

Key rules:
- Two-family dwelling use is subject to R2 Zone regulations, not RS1 Zone regulations.
- Townhouse use is subject to RT1 Zone regulations, not RS1 Zone regulations.
- Per new single-family lot: $6,000 General Amenity and $1,000 Affordable Housing Reserve Fund.
- Per new lot less than 550 m2 or half duplex: $3,960 General Amenity and $660 Affordable Housing Reserve Fund.
- Per new townhouse unit: $3,660 General Amenity and $610 Affordable Housing Reserve Fund.

Who it affects: The amendment applies to the specified portions of the four properties at 3420 Luxton Road, 1120 Finney Road, and 3219 and 3235 Loledo Place.

Portions of the properties at 3208 and 3212 Happy Valley Rd are moved from the Rural Residential 2 (RR2) Zone to the Residential Townhouse 1 (RT1) Zone. The bylaw also sets amenity contributions for each townhouse unit on these properties and says they are not eligible for a reduction under Section 2 of Schedule AD.

Key rules:
- Only the portions shaded on Plan No. 1 are rezoned.
- The rezoned land changes from RR2 to RT1.
- Amenity contribution: 3,660 per townhouse unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
- Amenity contribution: $610 per townhouse unit towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund.
- These contributions are marked “No” for eligibility for reduction under Section 2 of Schedule AD.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to the specified portions of 3208 and 3212 Happy Valley Rd and to townhouse units on those portions.

The listed properties on Arncote Avenue, Peatt Road and Sunderland Road are rezoned from One- and Two-Family Residential (R2) to City Centre Pedestrian (CCP). The bylaw also sets amenity contributions for new residential units and commercial space created on these properties; the contributions are not eligible for reduction under Section 2 of Schedule AD.

Key rules:
- General Amenity Reserve Fund: $2,850 per new unit on storeys 1–4; $1,425 on storeys 5–6; $712.50 on storey 7 or higher.
- Affordable Housing Reserve Fund: $750 per new unit on storeys 1–4; $375 on storeys 5–6; $187.50 on storey 7 or higher.
- Commercial space: $10.75 per square metre towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
- Amenity contributions are marked “No” for eligibility for reduction under Section 2 of Schedule AD.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to the listed properties at 808, 812 and 820 Arncote Avenue; 2630, 2636, 2640 and 2646 Peatt Road; and 2633, 2637, 2641 and 2647 Sunderland Road.

The shaded portions of 3216 Happy Valley Road are changed from the Rural Residential (RR2) Zone to the Residential Townhouse 1 (RT1) Zone. Development on this property may have a floor area ratio of up to 1.5 if the required contribution is paid before a building permit is issued, and buildings or structures may not exceed 3 storeys.

Key rules:
- The rezoning applies to the portions shown shaded on Plan No. 1.
- Maximum floor area ratio may be increased to 1.5 if the required amount is paid before a building permit is issued.
- $3,660 per townhouse unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
- $610 per townhouse unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
- No building or structure may exceed a height of 3 storeys.

Who it affects: This bylaw applies to owners and developers of the specified property at 3216 Happy Valley Road.

A secondary suite in a one-family dwelling is added as a permitted use on the specified lots at 1950 and 1991 Bear Mountain Parkway, subject to Section 3.08. The amendment also sets a 1.5 m (4.9 ft) interior side-lot-line provision for those lots and replaces Schedule O-2 with a new map.

Key rules:
- Secondary suites in one-family dwellings are subject to Section 3.08.
- The changes apply to the specified lots at 1950 and 1991 Bear Mountain Parkway.
- The amendment specifies a distance of 1.5 m (4.9 ft) from an interior side lot line.
- Schedule O-2 is replaced by the map in Schedule A.

Who it affects: Owners and residents of the specified lots at 1950 and 1991 Bear Mountain Parkway.

Portions of six properties on Peatt Road and Scafe Road are moved from the One- and Two-Family Residential (R2) Zone to the City Centre Pedestrian (CCP) Zone. New residential units and commercial space created on the affected lands are subject to amenity contributions at the rates below.

Key rules:
- Portions of the six properties are rezoned from R2 to CCP.
- General Amenity Reserve Fund: $2,850 per new residential unit on the 1st to 4th storeys; $1,425 on the 5th and 6th storeys; $712.50 on the 7th storey or higher.
- Affordable Housing Reserve Fund: $750 per new residential unit on the 1st to 4th storeys; $375 on the 5th and 6th storeys; $187.50 on the 7th storey or higher.
- Commercial space created is subject to $10.75 per square metre towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
- These amenity contributions are not eligible for reduction under Section 2 of Schedule AD.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to owners and developers of the affected portions of 2746 Peatt Road and 2739, 2743, 2747, 2749 and 2751 Scafe Road.

Specified portions of 621 and 629 Rockingham Road are changed from the One- and Two-Family Residential (R2) Zone to the Residential Small Lot (RS1) Zone. For creating a single-family lot less than 550 m2, the bylaw lists amenity contributions of $3,960 to the General Amenity Reserve Fund and $660 to the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; these contributions are not eligible for reduction under Section 2 of Schedule AD.

Key rules:
- The zoning change applies to the portions shown shaded on Plan No. 1.
- 621 Rockingham Road changes from R2 to RS1.
- 629 Rockingham Road changes from R2 to RS1.
- The listed General Amenity Reserve Fund contribution is $3,960.
- The listed Affordable Housing Reserve Fund contribution is $660.
- The contributions are marked “No” for eligibility for reduction under Section 2 of Schedule AD.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to the specified portions of the properties at 621 and 629 Rockingham Road.

Portions of 640 and 644 Granderson Road are moved from the One- and Two-Family Residential (R2) Zone to the City Centre (CC1) Zone. New residential units on these properties are subject to amenity contributions that vary by storey, with contributions paid to the General Amenity Reserve Fund and Affordable Housing Reserve Fund.

Key rules:
- For each new unit on the 1st to 4th storeys: $2,850 to the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
- For each new unit on the 5th and 6th storeys: $1,425 to the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
- For each new unit on the 1st to 4th storeys: $750 to the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund.
- For each new unit on the 5th and 6th storeys: $375 to the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund.
- These amenity contributions are not eligible for reduction under Section 2 of Schedule AD.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to the portions shown on Plan No. 1 of 640 and 644 Granderson Road.

The portions shown on Plan No. 1 of 2762, 2768, and 2774 Winster Road are rezoned from One- and Two-Family Residential (R2) to City Centre 1 (CC1). New residential units on those portions are subject to amenity contributions based on the storey where they are created, and the contributions are not eligible for reduction under Section 2 of Schedule AD.

Key rules:
- The rezoning applies only to the portions shown shaded on Plan No. 1.
- Per new unit on the 1st to 4th storeys: $2,850 General Amenity and $750 Affordable Housing Reserve Funds.
- Per new unit on the 5th and 6th storeys: $1,425 General Amenity and $375 Affordable Housing Reserve Funds.
- Per new unit on the 7th storey or higher: $712.50 General Amenity and $187.50 Affordable Housing Reserve Funds.
