At 646 Atkins Avenue, the bylaw changes the property’s zoning from R2 (One- and Two-Family Residential) to RS1 (Residential Small Lot). It also changes parking requirements for certain residential lots in a Restricted Zone and sets amenity contributions for development on the rezoned property.

Key rules:
- Restricted Zone lots shown on Schedule AA with an area of 281 m2 or greater require 0 spaces per dwelling unit.
- Developed Restricted Zone lots under 281 m2 require 1 space per dwelling unit.
- Townhouse units: $610 per unit for the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund and $3,660 per unit for the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
- Single family homes or half duplexes: $660 per unit for the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund and $3960 per unit for the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
- The amenity contributions are not eligible for a reduction under Section 2 of Schedule AD.

Who it affects: The bylaw affects the owner or developer of 646 Atkins Avenue and people developing residential uses on the specified Restricted Zone lots.

Public Assembly and Entertainment Uses are added as a listed use in Section 6.91.01(3) of the CD2 Zone. The amendment does not specify further conditions or define these uses in the text provided.

Key rules:
- Adds “Public Assembly and Entertainment Uses” to Section 6.91.01(3)(g).
- Subsequent clauses are renumbered accordingly.

Who it affects: This amendment applies to properties in the CD2 Zone.

The amendment allows secondary suites within townhomes on the property at 1234 Goldstream Avenue, in accordance with Section 3.08. It also updates the bylaw’s definitions of “secondary suite” and “suite.”

Key rules:
- A secondary suite is an accessory dwelling unit within a one-family dwelling, two-family dwelling, or townhouse unit, as permitted in Part 6.
- “Suite” means a secondary suite, garden suite, or carriage suite.
- Secondary suites within townhomes are added for the property at 1234 Goldstream Avenue, in accordance with Section 3.08.

Who it affects: The amendment applies to the property legally described as Lot 1 Sections 85 and 116 Esquimalt District Plan 21226 (1234 Goldstream Avenue).

The five properties at 2830 Jacklin Road and 2825, 2827, 2829, and 2831 Knotty Pine Road are rezoned from One- and Two-Family Residential (R2) to City Centre Pedestrian (CCP). The bylaw sets a maximum building height of 6-storeys and specifies amenity contributions for residential units and commercial space created on these properties.

Key rules:
- Maximum permitted height: 6-storeys.
- $2,850 per residential unit on the 1st to 4th storeys for the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
- $1,425 per residential unit on the 5th and 6th storeys for the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
- $750 per residential unit on the 1st to 4th storeys and $375 on the 5th and 6th storeys for the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund.
- $10.75 per square meter of commercial space created for the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
- Eligible for reduction in Section 2 of Schedule AD: No.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to the properties at 2830 Jacklin Road and 2825, 2827, 2829, and 2831 Knotty Pine Road.

Section 6, “City Centre Neighbourhoods,” is removed from Appendix J of the Langford Zoning Bylaw, 1999. The amendment does not state any replacement text or other changes.

Key rules:
- Section 6 – City Centre Neighbourhoods of Appendix J is deleted.

Who it affects: This amendment applies to people and properties governed by the Langford Zoning Bylaw, 1999.

A place of worship is added as a permitted “Other” use for the specified property at 2750 Leigh Road. The amendment adds this use to the property’s MUE1 zoning text.

Key rules:
- Adds “Place of Worship” as an “Other” use at 2750 Leigh Road.

Who it affects: This amendment applies to the specified property at 2750 Leigh Road.

The property at 1029 Marwood Avenue is moved from the RR2 (Rural Residential 2) Zone to the RS1 (Residential Small Lot) Zone. For this property, the bylaw allows a subdivision minimum lot area of 200 m² (2,153 ft²), with amenity contributions listed for new lots under 550m².

Key rules:
- The property is rezoned from RR2 to RS1.
- The minimum lot area for subdivision may be 200 m² (2,153 ft²) for the listed property.
- A contribution of $660 per new lot under 550m² goes to the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund.
- A contribution of $3,960 per new lot under 550m² goes to the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
- The listed property is not eligible for the reduction in Section 2 of Schedule AD.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to the owner of 1029 Marwood Avenue and anyone proposing subdivision of that property.

A school is added as a permitted use under Section 6.69C.01 of Langford Zoning Bylaw No. 300, 1999. The bylaw title identifies 691 Kodiak Way.

Key rules:
- Adds “School” to the permitted uses in Section 6.69C.01.
- Amends Langford Zoning Bylaw No. 300, 1999.
- The bylaw title names 691 Kodiak Way.

Who it affects: It affects people considering uses governed by Section 6.69C.01, identified in the bylaw title with 691 Kodiak Way.

A 0.130 ha (13,993.08 ft2) portion of Aldwynd Road identified as “Closed Road” is authorized to be closed to traffic and removed from public highway status. The closure takes effect when the Road Closure Plan and other required documents are deposited in the Victoria Land Title Office.

Key rules:
- The affected area is 0.130 ha (13,993.08 ft2).
- The area is identified as “Closed Road” on the Road Closure Plan.
- The road closes to public traffic on deposit of the plan and other closure documents in the Victoria Land Title Office.
- Once deposited, the area ceases to be public highway and its highway dedication is cancelled.

Who it affects: This bylaw affects people who use the portion of Aldwynd Road identified as “Closed Road” on the Road Closure Plan.

Building work in Langford—from new construction and alterations to demolition, repairs and changes in occupancy—is subject to this bylaw’s rules on permits, owner responsibilities, inspections and compliance. Its sections also cover site services and access, pools, professional review, energy requirements, offences and penalties; appendices provide permit-fee schedules and technical drawings.

Key rules:
- Owners must obtain required permits or approvals and pay fees and deposits before work begins.
- Permit applications are filed online through the City of Langford EPR Portal.
- Owners must give at least 24 hours’ notice for required field inspections.
- An occupancy permit is required before occupancy after construction, partial demolition, alteration or a change in occupancy.
- A permit or City review does not remove the owner’s responsibility to comply with the bylaw and Building Code.
- Appendix A contains fee schedules; Appendix B contains technical drawings for drainage, sewer connections and driveway access.

Who it affects: Owners and people planning or carrying out building or plumbing work covered by the bylaw in Langford.

The bylaw establishes and governs Langford’s municipal water and energy services, including service applications, connections, use, fees, payment, and enforcement. It is organised around service areas and separate water and energy terms, with schedules covering connections, rates, charges, and other service details.

Key rules:
- The City may provide services directly or through another person or organization.
- Applicants must pay the applicable application and connection fees set out in the schedules.
- Required security may not be less than $50 or exceed estimated bills for the two highest consecutive Months.
- Services may be discontinued for unpaid charges or non-compliance, after not less than 48 hours' written notice stating the reasons.
- The City or Service Provider may enter properties or buildings connected to, using, or required to apply for services to inspect compliance.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to applicants, customers, and residential, commercial, industrial or institutional properties within the applicable water and energy service areas.

Rules for using Langford’s streets and City-controlled or City-owned parking lots cover traffic, vehicles, stopping, cycling and micromobility, and parking. The bylaw is organized into five parts: street use and vehicle regulations; traffic controls; parking; permits and licences; and administration, including officer authority and enforcement.

Key rules:
- Applies to all highways vested in the City and City-controlled or City-owned parking lots, except as otherwise provided.
- Rules cover street use, stopping and idling, cycles and other devices, vehicle regulations, heavy trucks, dangerous goods, impoundment, and parking.
- Part 4 sets out permit and licence processes for events, vehicles and routes, street use and construction, patios, and street work.
- Part 5 covers officer authority, contraventions, enforcement, and general administration.

Who it affects: It applies to people using Langford’s streets and City-controlled or City-owned parking lots, and to people applying for the permits or licences it covers.

Most signs in Langford need a permit, and the rules limit where signs can go, their size and height, and which types are allowed. Requirements vary by sign type and zone; some signs are exempt from permits, while others are prohibited.

Key rules:
- Most signs require a permit before they are erected, placed, constructed, altered or relocated; listed exceptions include political signs and qualifying temporary real-estate signs.
- Signs projecting over pedestrian areas need at least 2.5m clearance; signs over areas used by vehicles need at least 4.5m clearance.
- A business may display no more than one sandwich board sign, with maximum dimensions of .6 m (2 ft) by .9 m (3 ft) per side.
- Temporary new business signs may remain for up to 60 days, with a possible renewal for a second 60-day period.
- Billboards and roof signs are prohibited; abandoned signs cannot remain in place for more than 60 days.
- A person who contravenes the bylaw is guilty of an offence and liable to penalties prescribed in the Offence Act.

Who it affects: The bylaw applies to people putting up or changing signs, and to owners or occupiers who maintain or allow signs on their property.

People requesting City services, documents, maps and RCMP records may pay the fees set out in updated Schedules A through E. The amendment replaces the previous schedules covering administration, finance, planning and development, mapping, and RCMP services.

Key rules:
- Single-sided photocopies cost $0.37 per page; double-sided copies cost $0.69 per sheet.
- A certificate of taxes and charges outstanding costs $31.00 electronically or $52.70 prepared by the City of Langford.
- Accounts outstanding beyond 30 days incur interest of 1.5% per month, compounded to an annual rate of 19.56%.
- Hard-copy maps 11x17 or smaller cost $6.80 each; electronic Adobe Format maps have no charge.
- The first collision report copy to ICBC, a driver, property owners, passengers, etc. has no charge; each additional copy costs $26.55.

Who it affects: The fees apply to residents, businesses, property owners and others requesting the listed City services, documents, maps or RCMP records.
